docs.title: milner
docs.text:
A benchmark harness for comparing memory strategies in LLM agents.

Run the same task through different memory designs under one standard configuration and get accuracy, token cost, latency and retrieval hit rate side by side, with every prompt and response logged to disk.

docs.title: Statement of need
docs.text:
Agent-memory work (rolling summaries, retrieval over past turns, long-context prompting) is usually evaluated with bespoke scripts: different prompts, models, scoring rules and cost accounting. Results are therefore hard to compare or reproduce, and the cost side is often missing: a summary strategy that makes a model call every few turns looks cheap if those calls are not counted.

milner provides the shared scaffolding: a memory interface, a model interface, a JSONL task schema, one metrics definition that charges memory overhead to the strategy, and config-driven, seeded, fully logged runs.

docs.title: What it is not
docs.text: It is not a new memory algorithm and not a new dataset. It is the harness that lets you compare algorithms on datasets, including ones you bring.

docs.title: Naming
docs.text: Named after Brenda Milner, whose studies of patient H.M. established that memory comprises distinct systems.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
One YAML file describes one experiment. Relative paths resolve against the config file, so it works from any directory.

name: my-experiment        # run directory name
seed: 0                    # passed to every model adapter
dataset: data.jsonl
output_dir: runs           # logs go to runs/<name>/
limit: null                # optionally only the first N examples
max_answer_tokens: 32

model:
  type: openai             # mock | openai | anthropic | hf
  model: gpt-4o-mini
  temperature: 0.0

memories:
  - type: none
  - type: full
    max_turns: null        # keep only the most recent N turns
  - type: retrieval
    top_k: 3
    embedder: {type: hashing, dim: 256}   # or {type: sentence-transformers, model: ...}
  - type: summary
    chunk_size: 10
    max_summary_words: 120
    label: rolling         # optional display name; labels must be unique

docs.title: Model adapters
docs.text: type Notes mock Deterministic offline stand-in. For harness checks and tests, not for science. openai Hosted API, or any OpenAI-compatible server through base_url (vLLM, llama.cpp, Ollama). anthropic Anthropic Messages API. hf In-process transformers; greedy decoding at temperature 0.

docs.title: Task schema
docs.text:
JSONL, one example per line.

Field Required Meaning id yes unique example id turns yes list of {turn_id, role, content}; turn_id defaults to t<index> question yes asked after the whole session is ingested answer yes gold answer evidence no turn_ids that contain the answer; enables the retrieval hit rate session_id no defaults to id

docs.title: Reproducibility
docs.text:
What milner does: fixes seeds and passes them to adapters, defaults to temperature 0, copies the resolved config beside the logs, rebuilds every table from the raw logs, and uses a hash embedder that is identical across processes.

What it cannot promise: hosted APIs may change models behind a name or ignore seed; transformers outputs can differ across hardware and library versions. Record the model version and library versions with your results; the per-example logs make differences inspectable.

docs.title: A new memory strategy
docs.text:
Subclass MemoryBackend, implement reset, add_turn and retrieve, and register it.

from milner import MemoryBackend, MemoryContext, register_memory


class LastN(MemoryBackend):
    def __init__(self, n=5, **kw):
        super().__init__(**kw)
        self.n, self.turns = n, []

    def reset(self):
        self.turns = []

    def add_turn(self, turn):
        self.turns.append(turn)

    def retrieve(self, question):
        kept = self.turns[-self.n :]
        return MemoryContext(self.render(kept), [t.turn_id for t in kept])


register_memory("last_n", LastN)

Then use it in YAML:

memories:
  - {type: last_n, n: 8}

Rules that keep comparisons fair:

  • The factory receives the experiment's model. If your strategy calls it, charge the tokens and latency to self.usage (see milner/memory/summary.py), or the strategy gets free compression.
  • Return retrieved_turn_ids when the context quotes source turns verbatim, and None when it does not, so the retrieval hit rate stays meaningful.

docs.title: A new model
docs.text: Subclass ModelAdapter, implement _complete(messages, max_tokens) returning (text, input_tokens, output_tokens), and register_model("name", YourClass).

docs.title: A new dataset
docs.text: Write a converter that yields milner.Example objects and milner.schema.dump_jsonl them. See milner/toy.py for a complete example.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
All metrics are computed from the raw per-example logs (<memory>.jsonl).

Metric Definition Accuracy Normalised gold answer appears as whole words in the prediction. Normalisation: lower-case, strip punctuation and the articles a/an/the. Exact match Normalised prediction equals normalised gold. Input tokens Mean per question: tokens in the answering prompt plus tokens of any model calls the memory made (for example summarisation). Output tokens Same, for generated tokens. Latency (s) Mean per question: the answering call plus wall-clock time spent ingesting turns and retrieving. Retrieval hit rate Mean fraction of an example's evidence turns present in the context. Strategies that keep no turn identity (summary) report - and are excluded rather than counted as zero.

Token counts come from the model adapter's reported usage. The mock model uses a simple word-and-punctuation estimate.

docs.title: Choosing a different scorer
docs.text: correct is whole-word containment, which suits short factual answers. For free-form answers, write the predictions out of the logs and score them with your own judge; the prediction and gold fields are in every record.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.text:
pip install "milner[plots]"
git clone https://github.com/rexthecoder/milner && cd milner
milner run examples/toy.yaml

The run uses the offline mock model, so it needs no GPU or API key. It prints a table and writes runs/toy/:

  • <memory>.jsonl: one record per example with the full prompt, response, token counts, latency and retrieved turns.
  • config.yaml: the exact config used.
  • summary.json, results.md, results.csv, plot.png.

Rebuild the table and figure from the raw logs at any time:

milner report runs/toy

docs.title: Using a real model
docs.text:
Start any OpenAI-compatible server (vLLM, llama.cpp's llama-server, Ollama) and use examples/openai_compatible.yaml:

pip install "milner[openai,embeddings,plots]"
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct
milner run examples/openai_compatible.yaml

For the hosted OpenAI API drop base_url and set OPENAI_API_KEY. For Anthropic use type: anthropic and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. For in-process inference use type: hf.

docs.title: Your own benchmark
docs.text: Convert it to JSONL (see Configuration) and point dataset: at the file. Validation errors name the file and line.
